text: A body of mass $0.5\mathrm{kg}$ travels on straight line path with velocity $v=\left (3x^{2}+4\right )\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}$. The net workdone by the force during its displacement from $x=0$ to $x=2\mathrm{m}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$v=3x^{2}+4$

at $x=0$, $v_{1}=4$ m/s

$x=2$, $v_{2}=16$ m/s

$\Rightarrow$ Work done = $\Delta$ kinetic energy

$=\frac{1}{2}\times m\left (v_{2}^{2}-v_{1}^{2}\right )$

$=\frac{1}{4}(256-16)$

$=60$ J

text: Two charged particles, having same kinetic energy, are allowed to pass through a uniform magnetic field perpendicular to the direction of motion. If the ratio of radii of their circular paths is $6:5$ and their respective masses ratio is $9:4$. Then, the ratio of their charges will be :

$\Rightarrow$ Ratio of radii $=\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}=\sqrt{\frac{m_{1}}{m_{2}}}\frac{q_{2}}{q_{1}}$

text: Time taken by light to travel in two different materials $A$ and $B$ of refractive indices $μ_{A}$ and $μ_{B}$ of same thickness is $t_{1}$ and $t_{2}$ respectively. If $t_{2}-t_{1}=5\times 10^{-10}$ s and the ratio of $μ_{A}$ to $μ_{B}$ is $1:2$. Then, the thickness of material, in meter is: (Given $v_{\mathrm{A}}$ and $v_{\mathrm{B}}$ are velocities of light in $A$ and $B$ materials respectively.)
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$t_{2}-t_{1}=5\times 10^{-10}$

$\Rightarrow \frac{d}{v_{B}}-\frac{d}{v_{A}}=5\times 10^{-10}$

and, $\frac{v_{B}}{v_{A}}=\frac{μ_{A}}{μ_{B}}=\frac{1}{2}$

$\Rightarrow d\left (1-\frac{v_{B}}{v_{A}}\right )=5\times 10^{-10}\times v_{B}$

$\Rightarrow d\left (1-\frac{1}{2}\right )=5\times 10^{-10}\times v_{B}$

$\Rightarrow d=10\times 10^{-10}\times v_{B}m$

$\Rightarrow d=5\times 10^{-10}\times v_{A}m$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text: A wire of length $\mathrm{L}$ and radius $\mathrm{r}$ is clamped rigidly at one end. When the other end of the wire is pulled by a force $\mathrm{F}$, its length increases by $5\mathrm{cm}$. solution.body:
$\frac{F/A}{\Delta L/L}=Y$

$\Rightarrow \Delta L=\frac{FL}{AY}$

$\frac{\Delta L_{2}}{\Delta L_{1}}=\left (\frac{F_{2}}{F_{1}}\right )\times \left (\frac{L_{2}}{L_{1}}\right )\times \left (\frac{A_{1}}{A_{2}}\right )$

text: A unit scale is to be prepared whose length does not change with temperature and remains $20\mathrm{cm}$, using a bimetallic strip made of brass and iron each of different length. The length of both components would change in such a way that difference between their lengths remains constant. If length of brass is $40\mathrm{cm}$, then length of iron will be $__________$ $\mathrm{cm}$. $\left (α_{\text{iron}}=1.2\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{K}^{-1} \right.$ and $\left. α_{\text{brass}}=1.8\times 10^{-5}\mathrm{K}^{-1}\right )$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let the brass length be $L_{b}=40\text{cm}$ and the iron length $L_{i}$. The difference $L_{i}-L_{b}$ stays constant at every temperature only if both strips expand by the same amount:

$\Delta L_{i}=\Delta L_{b}\Rightarrow α_{i}L_{i}\Delta T=α_{b}L_{b}\Delta T\Rightarrow α_{i}L_{i}=α_{b}L_{b}$

$L_{i}=\dfrac{α_{b}}{α_{i}}L_{b}=\dfrac{1.8\times 10^{-5}}{1.2\times 10^{-5}}\times 40=60\text{cm}$

The constant difference $L_{i}-L_{b}=60-40=20\text{cm}$ is the length of the unit scale.

Hence, the answer is 60.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift

text:
The volume charge density of a sphere of radius $6\mathrm{m}$ is $2~μ\mathrm{C}\qquad \mathrm{cm}^{-3}$. The number of lines of force per unit surface area coming out from the surface of the sphere is $_______________$ $\times 10^{10}\mathrm{NC}^{-1}$.

[Given : Permittivity of vacuum $𝜖_{0}=8.85\times 10^{-12}\mathrm{C}^{2}\mathrm{N}^{-1}-\mathrm{m}^{-2}$ ]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2022 (Online) 25th July Morning Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$ρ$ = 2 $μC/cm^{3}$

R = 6 m

Number of lines of force per unit area = Electric field at surface.

$=\frac{KQ}{R^{2}}$

$=\frac{1}{4πε_{0}}\frac{ρ\frac{4}{3}πR^{3}}{R^{2}}$

$=\frac{ρR}{3\in _{0}}$

$=\frac{2\times 10^{-6}\times 10^{6}\times 6}{3\times 8.85\times 10^{-12}}$

$=0.45197\times 10^{12}$

$=45.19\times 10^{10}$ N/C

$\simeq 45\times 10^{10}$
